items.title: Jay Leonhart interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I’ve had a chance to work with everybody... Sebesky and Phil Woods.

ctx.x: Yeah. Sure. I mean I know guys, very good musicians who at times in their lives really felt that they played much better drunk, high, whatever. And I understand that. I understand that. But it’s hard to last like that. It’s very tough on your system. And drinking is a perilous thing because it really takes it out of you. And you have that one little drink and just that one little drink, and you’re in the club and somebody wants to buy you another and you say, oh, no, I’ve had my drink. Oh, no, no. Of course…
Good words. The list of people you’ve played with since then is most impressive: Gerry Mulligan you played with, Sebesky and Phil Woods.

Yup, yup. Well being in New York and being in the studios, and being available, really available, I’ve had a chance to work with everybody. I mean just about everybody. I mean Miles Davis was one of the few I didn’t work with, I could name a small list of people who I never got a chance to play with.
